transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lara Patel (Head of ML - Orpheus), Omar Fadel (CTO), Sophie Nguyen (Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on success metrics for a 2-week pilot: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring buckets, and a nominal load run. Agreed to share artifacts and schedule a 5-day benchmark run mid-September.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria (latency, throughput, hallucination thresholds, accuracy buckets)
- Data and load sizing (sample counts, traffic shape)
- Golden prompt creation and acceptance process
- Regression and hallucination test design, scoring approach
- Operational requirements (SSO, audit logs, encryption)
- Timeline and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, well kick off on time. Diego and I are the Redwood side. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Lara Patel: Lara here, Omar and Sophie also on. Thanks Maya.
[00:12] Diego Ramos: hi all, Diego from Redwood infra team. real quick agenda is to map acceptance criteria and the benchmark steps for the pilot.
[00:22] Omar Fadel: good, we want low risk first, our main red lines are PII handling and latency under 400ms p99 if possible for short replies. longer sequences ok to be slower.
[00:35] Sophie Nguyen: and were concerned about hallucinations in our extraction pipeline, even small false positives cause downstream rework.
[00:44] Maya Chen: understood. Our usual approach: define golden prompts (a few canonical queries per intent), create a regression suite, then run head-to-head benchmarks across candidate models + configurations. we include hallucination detection checks and format validators.
[01:05] Diego Ramos: just to titrate expectations: for hosted redwood we can hit ~200-300ms median with our smaller quantized models, p99s depend on sequence length and batching. Dedicated pools give more predictable p99s. also note KV cache can help if you have repeated prefixes but we often see K-V cache mis-transcribed in notes so apologies.
[01:25] Lara Patel: can you clarify scoring? we want a mix of automated metrics + human labeling for edge cases.
[01:32] Diego Ramos: yes, proposed scoring: automated exact/slot match for structure tasks, BLEU/ROUGE-ish for free text with thresholds, then a human review bucket for 10-15% of edge outputs. we also recommend a hallucination flagging heuristic: factual inconsistency detector + out-of-domain pattern matcher.
[01:52] Sophie Nguyen: human review is expensive. how big does the regression set need to be?
[01:56] Maya Chen: typical starter is 500 gold prompts (50 intents x 10 variants) + 200 edge cases you call-out; for load we use 1k queries for a nominal soak and 10k for stress. since youre focused on precision, we can bias sample towards known trick cases.
[02:16] Omar Fadel: timeline? were aiming for a decision within 6 weeks.
[02:20] Maya Chen: pilot schedule we usually do: week 0 prep + dataset handoff, week 1 warm-up + golden prompt tuning, week 2 full 5-day benchmark (functional + load), then 1 week of result analysis and playbook handoff. that fits a 4-week active window but allow for buffer to 6.
[02:41] Diego Ramos: technical note on benchmarks: we run three passes - functional correctness (golden set, regression), latency/throughput (nominal load pattern and stress), and robustness (perturbed inputs, OCR mistakes, truncated contexts). each pass has deterministic seed for reproducibility and we record token-level timings for tracing.
[03:06] Lara Patel: about hallucination detection - can you show an example rule set?
[03:10] Diego Ramos: sure, example heuristics: presence of unsupported entities, improbable numeric claims, source-less factual assertions. we also run model-agnostic validators that check required fields/format; any output that fails structure goes to fail-fast path.
[03:26] Sophie Nguyen: what about privacy: are logs retained? we need KMS + optional log redaction and audit export to our S3.
[03:34] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS, audit logs, and you can toggle retention. for hosted pilot we can enable short retention and encrypted exports; full SOC2 docs will be in the security deck.
[03:50] Omar Fadel: for load shape, we typically have weekend spikes at end-of-month. can we simulate bursty traffic?
[03:56] Diego Ramos: absolutely, we model both poisson steady-state and burst profiles (90/10 split) and sample different sequence length distributions. well provide the harness so your SREs can inspect.
[04:10] Lara Patel: scoring thresholds: what do you suggest for acceptance?
[04:14] Maya Chen: suggested gates: functional pass rate >= 95% on golden prompts, hallucination rate <= 1% on sampled outputs, p50 latency < 250ms and p99 < 400ms for nominal payloads, and <5% regression vs baseline (your incumbent). those are starting points — you can tighten based on product needs.
[04:37] Sophie Nguyen: we need a way to triage failures quickly. is there a dashboard?
[04:41] Diego Ramos: Redwood Console will surface per-prompt failures, token-level cost breakdown, and a regression diff tool with side-by-side outputs. we can add custom labels for severity.
[04:55] Omar Fadel: on model variants — if dedicated capacity isnt provisioned, will we automatically fallback to a compatible hosted variant?
[05:02] Maya Chen: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible quantized variant; we can codify the fallback policy in the rollout config. that will affect latency/cost numbers which well show in the benchmark report.
[05:18] Lara Patel: on golden prompts creation - do you help author them or do we supply?
[05:22] Maya Chen: hybrid approach works best. we provide templates and some prefilled candidates, you provide domain-specific variations and we iterate. typically we converge in 3 cycles.
[05:32] Sophie Nguyen: for regression tests, do you store outputs for diffs?
[05:36] Diego Ramos: yes, we snapshot outputs and produce diffs; we also compute a regression score (weighted by intent criticality) and flag any output with hallucination or format violation.
[05:48] Omar Fadel: what about cost modeling for prod — can we get per-1000 token estimates at current config?
[05:52] Maya Chen: Diego will include a cost appendix with per-token estimates for the benchmarked configs — hosted vs dedicated and quantization levels.
[05:59] Lara Patel: ok next steps are clear. can we capture the success criteria in a one-pager for sign-off?
[06:05] Maya Chen: yes well draft a pilot acceptance one-pager that lists gates, dataset, owners, and timeline.
[06:11] Diego Ramos: quick clarifications on the load run: we need a 4-hour warm up, then 5 full days of business-hour traffic and two stress bursts; please confirm maintenance windows.
[06:24] Sophie Nguyen: we can give a 72-hour window for the run week and will flag our monthly spike day in advance.
[06:30] Omar Fadel: any blockers on security review?
[06:33] Maya Chen: none immediate. we will share SOC2 summary and our standard data processing addendum; for VPC/private we can present network architecture in the security session.
[06:44] Lara Patel: about labeling edge cases — we will propose an initial list of 200 edge samples, but may expand.
[06:50] Diego Ramos: recommended to include boundary sequences, non-English fragments, truncated inputs, and spurious punctuation.
[06:58] Maya Chen: great, Aaron (note: not on call) will send the shared folder links after the call.
[07:04] Omar Fadel: small thing — include a regression threshold per-intent, not just global, that helps our product owners.
[07:10] Maya Chen: good point, well include per-intent stretch goals.
[07:15] Lara Patel: final ask: can we get a sample scoring rubric for human reviewers?
[07:19] Diego Ramos: yes, well provide a 10-point rubric: correctness, completeness, hallucination, toxicity, format, latency note, confidence score, provenance tag, entity fidelity, and actionable suggestion.
[07:36] Maya Chen: recap of owners and dates: Maya share pricing/security (9/1), Diego upload harness + cost appendix (9/2), Sophie send samples (9/3), schedule bench week (confirm by 9/7).
[07:50] Omar Fadel: thanks all.
[07:52] Lara Patel: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
